area_summary: Most urgent: android.yml publishes android-latest on a push to any branch, on any tag push, and on settings-only files that are not in the APK. It has already shipped unmerged code to friends four times (runs 2/6/9/11 on claude/sharp-faraday-028jsr), and runs 4 and 5 hit a real publish race (HTTP 404 then 422). Fix it in the same push as this run's changes: otherwise pushing claude/charming-goodall-c84gcl will itself republish an unmerged APK to every phone. windows.yml has no version or tag guard, so a run can finish green with nothing released, and the tag lands on the wrong commit. Its 'lock not up to date' premise is false: the lock is in sync and npm ci works. Caching would save only seconds (install measured at 14 s). The DEFAULT_SERVER build env it sets has no effect. The docs still describe the Railway setup: there is no Fly config in the repo, the Railway deploy steps are wrong now, the 'set DEFAULT_SERVER before building' step does nothing, and the docs wrongly say Windows updates itself. Release stats show 786 checks of v1.5.1's latest.yml but zero downloads of the 1.5.x installer or blockmap. Packaging: the portable exe has had 3 downloads ever and its autostart is broken. 53 unused Chromium locale packs add about 41 MB. Electron 33 and Node 20 are end-of-life. syncWebAssets can silently ship a dead Android overlay, and the Android versionName never changes, so the app offers 'v1.6.0' to users already on v1.6.0. All proposals keep the wire protocol unchanged.

findings.title: APK workflow republishes android-latest from any branch or tag push and for files not in the APK; parallel publishes race
findings.evidence: android.yml:7-11 has only a `paths` filter (no `branches`), so any branch push runs it, and per GitHub docs every tag push too (path filters are not evaluated for tags), e.g. the `v*` tags windows.yml:10-12 suggests. :77-86 then always deletes and recreates android-latest. Actions history: 12 runs, 7 on claude/sharp-faraday-028jsr; runs 2/6/9/11 shipped unmerged code to android-latest before main re-published. Concurrency is per ref (:18): runs 4 (branch) and 5 (main) published in the same seconds (09:48:20-24); run 4 died with `HTTP 404 Reference does not exist` then `HTTP 422 Published releases must have a valid tag`. `memedrop/overlay/src/**` also matches settings.html/settings.js, never copied into the APK (build.gradle.kts:12-14). Each publish bumps versionCode, so Updater.kt:58 offers every phone an 'update' at next app open.
findings.proposed_change:
on:
  push:
    branches: ['**']   # branches seulement : un tag v1.2.3 (release Windows) ne republie pas l'APK
    paths:
      - 'memedrop/android/**'
      # seuls fichiers de overlay/src copiés dans l'APK (syncWebAssets)
      - 'memedrop/overlay/src/overlay.js'
      - 'memedrop/overlay/src/overlay.html'
      - 'memedrop/overlay/src/styles.css'
      - '.github/workflows/android.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:
concurrency:
  group: android-apk-${{ github.ref }}
  # main : ne jamais couper une publication entre delete et create
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
...
      - name: Publish to the android-latest release
        # les branches de travail compilent (artefact) mais ne publient pas
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
Optional hardening: when the release exists, `gh release upload android-latest MemeDrop.apk --clobber`, then `gh release upload android-latest version.json --clobber` and `gh release edit android-latest --notes ...` instead of delete+create (create only if missing), so a failed/cancelled publish never leaves friends without android-latest. Update memedrop/README.md:140-144 ('every push to main').
findings.behavior_change: bugfix: only main builds reach friends' phones; feature branches, tag pushes and settings-only commits no longer republish the APK or trigger a bogus update prompt
findings.cross_component: memedrop/README.md:140-144; android/app/build.gradle.kts:12-14 (the paths list must mirror the files syncWebAssets copies)
findings.risk: Low. Branch pushes still build and upload the APK artifact for testing; shipping a branch build to phones now requires merging to main. Land this in the same commit as (or before) any push of this run touching memedrop/android or memedrop/overlay/src: GitHub uses the workflow file of the pushed commit, otherwise pushing claude/charming-goodall-c84gcl itself republishes an unmerged APK to every friend.
findings.value: Stops unreviewed code from auto-reaching every Android friend, removes the observed publish race and spurious update prompts; one publish per merged change instead of two.

findings.title: Windows release run can go green without releasing anything, accepts a tag that doesn't match package.json, and tags the wrong commit
findings.evidence: Nothing checks that overlay/package.json was bumped. If v$VERSION is already published, electron-builder 24 (default releaseType draft) only warns 'GitHub release not created' (existing type not compatible with publishing type), skips the uploads and exits 0; then :47-50 `gh release edit "v$VERSION" --draft=false --latest --title ... --notes ...` rewrites that old release. Green run, nothing shipped (unbumped releases already happened: see a01401a message about 1.4.3/1.4.4). A pushed tag (:10-12) is never compared with package.json. electron-builder creates the draft without target_commitish (releases show target_commitish 'main'), so publishing tags the default-branch HEAD, not the built commit: a dispatch from another branch ships that branch's code tagged on main. No concurrency group (tag push + manual run share one draft).
findings.proposed_change:
jobs:
  release:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    concurrency:
      group: windows-release
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps (after setup-node, before npm):
      - name: Check version
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          VERSION=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")
          if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" = tag ] && [ "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" != "v$VERSION" ]; then
            echo "::error::Tag $GITHUB_REF_NAME ≠ package.json (v$VERSION)"; exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$(gh release view "v$VERSION" --json isDraft -q .isDraft 2>/dev/null)" = false ]; then
            echo "::error::v$VERSION déjà publiée : augmente la version dans overlay/package.json"; exit 1
          fi
Publish step: `gh release edit "v$VERSION" --target "$GITHUB_SHA" --draft=false --latest ...` (target is ignored when the tag already exists, e.g. tag-triggered runs). A leftover draft from a failed run still passes the guard and is reused by electron-builder.
findings.behavior_change: bugfix: an unbumped or mismatched release now fails loudly instead of going green and rewriting an existing release; the tag lands on the built commit
findings.risk: Low. Re-running a release for an already published version is refused on purpose (a published latest.yml and its binaries must not change under clients).
findings.value: Prevents silent no-op releases (owner believes friends got a fix) and source/binary tag mismatches.

findings.title: Docs and release notes say Windows installs update themselves; they only update if the user opens the settings (no 1.5.x download so far)
findings.evidence: overlay/main.js:543 `autoUpdater.autoDownload = false`; the 30-min checks (:856-857) only set updateState. Downloading needs a click in the settings window, which is not opened when the app starts at login (:817-830), and nothing (tray, OS notification) signals the update. Yet ../README.md:56 « se met à jour automatiquement », windows.yml:50 « Les PC déjà équipés se mettent à jour tout seuls », RELEASE.md:53 « Tes potes vont recevoir la notif ». Release stats (read-only GitHub API): since 2026-09-24, v1.5.1's latest.yml was fetched 786 times but MemeDrop-Setup-1.5.1.exe and its .blockmap 0 times (same for 1.5.0; v1.4.4 had 5/5): no client has pulled 1.5.x.
findings.proposed_change: Docs only (no behavior change): ../README.md:56 → « MemeDrop se lance ensuite tout seul au démarrage (icône dans la barre des tâches) et te signale les mises à jour : clic sur l'icône → réglages → Télécharger → Installer & redémarrer. » windows.yml:50 notes → « ... Les PC déjà équipés la proposent dans les réglages de l'app (Télécharger → Installer & redémarrer). ... » RELEASE.md:53 → same wording. Optional code (overlay/main.js, visible, owner's call): in autoUpdater.on('update-available'), when the check was not manual and info.version was not yet announced, `tray?.displayBalloon({ iconType: 'info', title: 'MemeDrop', content: `Mise à jour v${info.version} disponible — clique pour l'installer` })`, with `tray.on('balloon-click', () => createSettingsWindow())` registered once in createTray; or `autoUpdater.autoDownload = true` so the existing autoInstallOnAppQuit installs at the next quit.
findings.behavior_change: none (docs); the optional code variant is visible (tray balloon or background download)
findings.risk: None for the docs. The balloon variant must fire once per version, not every 30 min.
findings.value: The owner currently assumes friends run the latest Windows build; they don't, which matters whenever a fix or bot change relies on new client code.

findings.title: 'Set DEFAULT_SERVER before building' is a no-op: self-hosted builds still connect to the owner's bot
findings.evidence: overlay/main.js:8-9 reads process.env.DEFAULT_SERVER at run time on the user's PC; electron-builder copies main.js verbatim (no bundler, no extraMetadata), so the variable set at build time by memedrop/README.md:90-106 (« main.js already reads from a build-time env var ... $env:DEFAULT_SERVER = "wss://memedrop-bot.up.railway.app" # YOUR Railway URL »), RELEASE.md:40 and windows.yml:38 changes nothing: every .exe defaults to wss://memedrop-bot.fly.dev. Anyone following « Héberger ton propre MemeDrop » ships an app that pairs with the owner's bot. The guide also claims the overlay « tries wss://memedrop-bot.up.railway.app by default » (:273) and never says Android has its own default (Prefs.kt:12).
findings.proposed_change: memedrop/README.md Part 2.1 (:90-106) → « Le serveur par défaut est une constante : DEFAULT_SERVER dans overlay/main.js (l. 8-9) et dans android/app/src/main/java/com/memedrop/app/Prefs.kt (l. 12). Pour ton propre bot, modifie ces deux lignes avant de compiler (ou saisis l'URL dans Réglages → « URL du serveur bot »). La variable d'environnement DEFAULT_SERVER n'agit qu'au lancement (dev : `DEFAULT_SERVER=ws://localhost:8765 npm start`, sur une config neuve). » Fix :273 (default is wss://memedrop-bot.fly.dev). Delete the dead `DEFAULT_SERVER:` line in windows.yml:38 and the `$env:DEFAULT_SERVER` line in RELEASE.md:40. Alternative if a real build-time setting is wanted: build with `npx electron-builder ... -c.extraMetadata.defaultServer="$DEFAULT_SERVER"` and read `process.env.DEFAULT_SERVER || require('./package.json').defaultServer || 'wss://memedrop-bot.fly.dev'` in main.js.
findings.cross_component: ../.github/workflows/windows.yml:38, RELEASE.md:40; overlay/main.js:8-9 only for the extraMetadata alternative
findings.risk: None (docs and a dead env line).
findings.value: Self-hosters stop shipping apps wired to the owner's server; the owner stops relying on a CI env var that does nothing.

findings.title: Technical guide documents a Railway deployment that no longer exists; the real Fly.io setup is nowhere in the repo
findings.evidence: Railway was dropped for Fly.io (a01401a « Railway coupé »; release v1.4.3 « le bot est passé de Railway à Fly.io »), yet memedrop/README.md only documents Railway: :8, diagram :18-33, all of Part 1 :37-82 (railway CLI, Variables tab, Generate Domain, wss://memedrop-bot.up.railway.app), :255, limitations :283-284, layout :297-298. The repo has no Fly config (no fly.toml/Dockerfile; only bot/railway.json, now dead, and nixpacks.toml), so prod can't be redeployed from the repo. Fly specifics that lose data/uptime are undocumented: store.json (favorites/groups/stats, store.js:16) lives on the Machine's ephemeral rootfs (reset on deploy) unless a volume is mounted and DATA_DIR points to it; with fly launch's default auto_stop_machines a stopped Machine means the bot is offline on Discord.
findings.proposed_change: 1) Commit the Fly config actually used in prod (bot/fly.toml, plus Dockerfile if any). It should contain: [http_service] internal_port = the port the bot listens on (PORT, else WS_PORT, else 8765), auto_stop_machines = 'off', min_machines_running = 1, a check on /health; [mounts] source = 'memedrop_data', destination = '/data' and [env] DATA_DIR = '/data'. If the start command chains deploy-commands.js, end it with `exec node index.js` so Fly's kill signal reaches node and store.flush() runs (index.js:1251-1259). 2) Rewrite memedrop/README.md for Fly: :8 and :18-33 ('on Fly.io'); Part 1.2 → `fly launch --no-deploy`, `fly secrets set DISCORD_TOKEN=... CLIENT_ID=... LINK_SECRET=...`, `fly volumes create memedrop_data --size 1`, `fly deploy`, URL wss://<app>.fly.dev; :255 'Local development'; :283-284 Railway → Fly volume; :297-298. 3) Delete bot/railway.json (or mark it legacy): unused, and the apps force-migrate Railway URLs anyway (see railway-url-migration-too-broad).
findings.risk: None for docs. Don't invent the app name/region: commit the owner's real config (`fly config save -a memedrop-bot` writes it to fly.toml).
findings.value: Makes the production deploy reproducible and prevents silent loss of favorites/groups/stats on redeploy.

findings.title: Overlay ships Electron 33 (Chromium 130), end-of-life since April 2025, while decoding untrusted media 24/7
findings.evidence: package.json:21 `"electron": "^33.4.11"` (lock: 33.4.11, the last 33.x). Electron supports only its latest three majors; 33 reached end-of-life on 2025-04-29, so this Chromium/V8 has had no security backports for about 18 months. The overlay runs all day on friends' gaming PCs and decodes attacker-chosen bytes: any non-blocked member of a linked server can /drop an image/GIF/video/audio of their choice (the bot only checks Discord's contentType, bot/index.js:514-516, 541-548) plus caption/username text. electron-builder ^24.13.3 is two majors behind as well.
findings.proposed_change: Not doable in this offline run (needs the npm registry to regenerate package-lock and a Windows machine to test). Track as a dedicated change: in overlay/, `npm i -D electron@<current supported major> electron-builder@latest`, commit package.json + lock, then test on Windows: transparent always-on-top overlay over a borderless game, click-through with setIgnoreMouseEvents forwarding and the cursor-polling drag, tray menu, settings window, electron-store data kept, and an electron-updater update from an installed 1.5.1. Bump the overlay version and release through windows.yml.
findings.cross_component: overlay/package-lock.json; overlay/main.js if a breaking API change hits
findings.risk: Medium: Electron majors carry breaking changes; must be tested on Windows; the first update after the bump is close to a full download.
findings.value: Restores Chromium/V8 security fixes on an always-running app that renders untrusted media.

findings.title: Server-URL migration rewrites every Railway URL, so a self-hoster on Railway is forced back to the owner's Fly bot
findings.evidence: main.js:14-16 tests `/\.up\.railway\.app/i` and :58 rewrites any matching saved serverUrl to DEFAULT_SERVER at every launch; Prefs.kt:24-28 ignores any Railway URL on read. The project only ever used memedrop-production-3106.up.railway.app (old default, a01401a^) and the placeholder memedrop-bot.up.railway.app (initial commit). A self-hoster on Railway (the deployment memedrop/README.md Part 1 still teaches) enters their URL in the settings and is silently switched back to wss://memedrop-bot.fly.dev at the next start (on Android the getter never even returns it).
findings.behavior_change: bugfix: a user-chosen Railway URL is kept; the owner's old URLs are still migrated
findings.risk: Low: a friend who typed some other Railway host by hand would no longer be auto-migrated (none known).
findings.value: Makes the documented self-hosting path work and keeps the user's setting authoritative.

findings.title: Portable build is shipped on every release but nearly unused, and its autostart is broken
findings.evidence: package.json:48-50,54-56 build an NSIS installer and a portable exe for each release (MemeDrop-Portable-1.5.1.exe = 82,038,629 B). Release stats: 3 portable downloads across all 12 Windows releases (all v1.2.1). electron-builder's portable launcher unpacks the app (~280 MB) into %TEMP%\<build id> at each launch and deletes it on exit, so process.execPath lives there; main.js:633 and :823-827 call setLoginItemSettings without `path`, so the Run key points at a file that is gone once the app quits: autostart (the 24/7 promise) silently fails for portable users, and electron-updater turns them into NSIS installs at the first update anyway.
findings.proposed_change: Preferred (release content change): windows.yml:39 → `npx electron-builder --win nsis --publish always`, and drop « (ou la version Portable) » from the notes (:50); keep package.json so `npm run build:portable` still works locally; update memedrop/README.md:113 and :192. One ~82 MB artifact and one NSIS packaging pass less per release. If the portable must stay instead: in main.js:633 and :823 pass `path: process.env.PORTABLE_EXECUTABLE_FILE || process.execPath` (env var set by electron-builder's portable launcher) to both setLoginItemSettings calls.
findings.behavior_change: visible: releases stop including MemeDrop-Portable-x.y.z.exe (alternative: bugfix, portable autostart works)
findings.cross_component: ../.github/workflows/windows.yml:39,50; memedrop/README.md:113,192; overlay/main.js:633,823 for the keep-portable alternative
findings.risk: Low: about zero users; an existing portable user keeps working and is migrated to NSIS by the updater.
findings.value: Smaller, simpler releases and no silently broken autostart.

findings.title: Every CI build gets a new versionCode but the same versionName, so the updater offers 'v1.6.0' to users running v1.6.0
findings.evidence: build.gradle.kts:36-37: versionCode = GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER but versionName is a hand-edited literal, and android.yml:66-67 re-derives versionName by grepping the Gradle file. Updater.kt:58 offers an update whenever versionCode grows, and app.js:56 then shows « Mise à jour disponible — v1.6.0 » / « Tu as la v1.6.0 ». It already happened: runs 9 (branch) and 10 (main) both published '1.5.3' (versionCodes 9 and 10), and 287abbd changed APK code without touching versionName. Renaming android.yml would also restart run_number at 1, so versionCode would go backwards (update never offered, install refused).
findings.proposed_change:
build.gradle.kts:
        // Ne pas renommer android.yml : GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER repartirait à 1 et les
        // APK suivants ne s'installeraient plus par-dessus (versionCode plus petit).
        val ciBuild = System.getenv("GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER")
        versionCode = (ciBuild ?: "1").toInt()
        versionName = "1.6.0" + (ciBuild?.let { " ($it)" } ?: "")
android.yml 'Rename APK + version.json': replace the grep by AGP's metadata so version.json always matches the APK:
          jq -c '{versionCode: .elements[0].versionCode, versionName: .elements[0].versionName}' \
            memedrop/android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/output-metadata.json > version.json
findings.behavior_change: visible: the app and its update card show the build number, e.g. « v1.6.0 (14) » (UX bugfix; old APKs just display the new string)
findings.risk: Low. jq is preinstalled on ubuntu runners; AGP writes output-metadata.json next to the APK (elements[0].versionCode/versionName, high confidence for AGP 8.5).
findings.value: Users and the owner can tell builds apart; version.json can no longer drift from the APK.

findings.title: syncWebAssets silently produces a broken Android overlay if overlay.html's script tag or a file name changes
findings.evidence: build.gradle.kts:15-20 injects android-shim.js by replacing the exact text `<script src="./overlay.js"></script>` (today overlay.html:443). Any edit of that tag on the Windows side (defer, quotes, path) turns the filter into a no-op without error; overlay.js then runs without window.memedrop (defined only by android-shim.js:11) and the Android overlay stops rendering drops, yet the build is green and android.yml auto-publishes it to every phone. A renamed overlay.js/styles.css is likewise just not copied. Copy (not Sync) also leaves stale files in build/generated/webassets for local incremental builds.
findings.behavior_change: none (a build that would ship a dead Android overlay now fails)
findings.cross_component: overlay/src/overlay.html:443 (the tag the filter depends on)
findings.value: Turns a silent, auto-published breakage of every Android overlay into a red build.

findings.title: Bot runtime pinned to Node 20, end-of-life since 2026-04-30
findings.evidence: bot/nixpacks.toml:2 `nixPkgs = ["nodejs_20"]` and windows.yml:29 `node-version: '20'`. Node 20 reached end-of-life on 2026-04-30 (no security releases since), while the bot is an internet-facing HTTP + WebSocket server (/, /health, /tts, WS upgrade). The bot only needs Node >= 18 APIs (global fetch, http, crypto; discord.js 14.26.4, ws 8.21.0); all bot files pass `node --check` under Node 22.23.4 here. Caveat: the repo doesn't show whether the Fly image is built from nixpacks.toml (no fly.toml/Dockerfile).
findings.proposed_change: bot/nixpacks.toml: `nixPkgs = ["nodejs_22"]` (Node 22 LTS, maintained until 2027-04-30). If Fly builds from a Dockerfile, use `FROM node:22-slim` there; check with `fly ssh console -C 'node -v'` after deploy. windows.yml:29 → `node-version: '22'` (build-time only). Update the layout comment memedrop/README.md:297 (« Node 20 LTS »).
findings.risk: Low: no Node-20-specific API is used; verify the bot boots and /drop + /tts work after deploy.
findings.value: Security patches for the only internet-facing component.

findings.title: Signing keys and .env are only ignored inside some subfolders of a public repo
findings.evidence: Only memedrop/android/.gitignore:7-9 ignores *.p12/*.keystore/*.jks, and .env is ignored only in bot/ and overlay/. memedrop/README.md:161 tells the owner to run `base64 -w0 memedrop-release.p12` without saying where the key lives; a key created at the repo root or in memedrop/ (or a stray .env holding DISCORD_TOKEN) is picked up by `git add -A` in this public repo. Precedent: the previous signing key was committed in clear (3a7989b) and remains in history.
findings.proposed_change:
New file /home/user/memedrop/.gitignore:
# Secrets : jamais commités, où qu'ils soient dans le repo
*.p12
*.jks
*.keystore
.env
(per-folder .gitignore files unchanged).
findings.risk: None: `git ls-files` lists no tracked file matching these patterns (.env.example is not matched).
findings.value: Cheap guard against leaking the Android update-signing key or the bot token.

findings.title: Windows release uses npm install on a false premise; the lock is in sync and npm ci works
findings.evidence: windows.yml:31-33 « npm install (pas npm ci) : le package-lock n'est pas toujours à jour ». Not true: overlay/package-lock.json packages[""] declares exactly package.json's dependencies/devDependencies and every locked version satisfies them (electron 33.4.11, electron-builder 24.13.3, electron-store 8.2.0, electron-updater 6.8.3, ws 8.21.0). Only packages[""].version is stale (1.1.0 vs 1.5.1, lock lines 3 and 9); npm ci builds the root node from package.json and its lockfile validation compares dependency versions only, so it accepts this lock (high confidence, npm 10/arborist). Measured 'Install dependencies' in both runs: 14-15 s, so cache: npm would save only seconds on a rarely run workflow.
findings.proposed_change:
-      # npm install (pas npm ci) : le package-lock n'est pas toujours à jour
-      - name: Install dependencies
-        run: npm install --no-audit --no-fund
+      # npm ci : installe exactement le package-lock (échoue s'il diverge de package.json)
+      - name: Install dependencies
+        run: npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
Optional: set lock lines 3 and 9 to "1.5.1" (or run `npm install --package-lock-only` next time the registry is reachable). Do not add caching: measured gain is negligible.
findings.behavior_change: none (same locked versions installed); a future package.json/lock divergence fails the release instead of silently resolving new versions
findings.risk: Very low; if the lock is ever left out of date, the release fails visibly and the fix is `npm install` + commit the lock.
findings.value: Reproducible, lock-verified release builds; removes a misleading comment.

findings.title: All 55 Chromium locale packs ship in the Windows app (~41 MB on disk, ~10 MB of the installer) for a French-only UI
findings.evidence: Measured from the official electron-v33.4.11-win32-x64.zip central directory (HTTP range read): locales/ holds 55 .pak files = 42.2 MB unpacked / 10.9 MB deflated, while fr.pak is 637 KB and en-US.pak 490 KB. The build config (package.json:24-68) has no electronLanguages, so all are packed into the 82 MB installer and the install dir. The UI is French and every date format call passes 'fr-FR' explicitly (settings.js:257,266,335); no code reads app.getLocale()/navigator.language.
findings.behavior_change: visible only on non-French, non-English Windows: Chromium-internal strings (native pickers, context menus) fall back to English
findings.risk: Low. The first update after the change is a larger differential download (archive layout changes).
findings.value: About 41 MB less on disk and about 10 MB less to download on first install (~12% of the installer).

findings.title: .env.example omits PUBLIC_BASE_URL and DATA_DIR: local/self-hosted bots send TTS through the owner's production server
findings.evidence: bot/index.js:577-581 builds the /tts links sent to overlays from PUBLIC_BASE_URL, else FLY_APP_NAME, else RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN, else the hard-coded https://memedrop-bot.fly.dev; store.js:16 reads DATA_DIR. Neither is in .env.example, so a local `npm start` (memedrop/README.md « Local development ») or any non-Fly/Railway host makes every overlay fetch TTS from the owner's production bot: local /tts changes can't be tested, another group's TTS texts reach the owner's server and consume its 30 req/min/IP budget (index.js:22-23). .env.example:7 also still says « Railway provides PORT automatically ».
findings.proposed_change:
Replace .env.example:7-8 and append (keep the file's English):
# HTTP + WebSocket port. PORT, when set, wins (Railway sets it; on Fly.io
# make fly.toml's internal_port match the port the bot listens on).
WS_PORT=8765
...
# Optional: public base URL of this bot, used for the /tts links sent to
# overlays. Auto-detected on Fly.io (FLY_APP_NAME) and Railway; anywhere
# else (local dev, VPS...) set it, or overlays fetch TTS from memedrop-bot.fly.dev.
# PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8765

# Optional: folder holding store.json (favorites, groups, stats). On Fly.io
# point it at a mounted volume (e.g. /data) or it is reset on every deploy.
# DATA_DIR=
findings.cross_component: memedrop/README.md « Local development » (:259-271) could mention PUBLIC_BASE_URL
findings.value: Correct local testing of TTS; self-hosters stop sending TTS text to the owner's bot.

findings.title: RELEASE.md still describes the manual pre-CI release flow with a never-expiring full-repo PAT
findings.evidence: RELEASE.md asks to create a classic PAT with full `repo` scope and « No expiration » (:13-19), build from a personal path C:\Users\tsumu\Downloads\... with $env:GH_TOKEN and the no-op DEFAULT_SERVER (:36-41), publish the draft by hand (:49-53), and says « Tes potes utilisent encore l'ancienne v1.0.0 » (:70-77), obsolete since 1.1.x. It never mentions windows.yml (publishes with GITHUB_TOKEN, no PAT), the Android release (android-latest, versionName to bump in build.gradle.kts:37), nor that overlay.js/overlay.html/styles.css are shared: a change reaches Android on the next push but Windows only after a version bump + Windows release.
findings.proposed_change: Rewrite RELEASE.md (French) around the workflows. Windows: 1) bump "version" in overlay/package.json; 2) merge to main; 3) Actions → « Windows release » → Run workflow (or `git tag vX.Y.Z && git push origin vX.Y.Z`); 4) friends see it in the settings within 30 min (Télécharger → Installer & redémarrer). Android: automatic on each push to main touching memedrop/android or overlay.js/overlay.html/styles.css → release android-latest; bump versionName in android/app/build.gradle.kts. Warn about the shared-renderer coupling. Keep a local build only as a fallback, with a fine-grained token (Contents read/write on this repo only, with an expiry) instead of a no-expiration classic `repo` PAT; drop the personal path, the DEFAULT_SERVER line and the v1.0.0 section.
findings.cross_component: depends on the final shape of android.yml/windows.yml
findings.value: Release doc matches reality; no long-lived broad token needed on the owner's PC.

findings.title: Guide and FRIENDS.md describe UI labels, files and behaviors that no longer exist
findings.evidence: memedrop/README.md: :193-195 « AWAITING LINK » / « LINKED », but the pill shows « en attente » / « connecté » (settings.js:405,411); :280 « To interact (close, drag), use the tray icon menu » contradicts :245-246 (drops have their own ✕ and drag); :290-329 layout lists android/app/memedrop-shared.keystore (deleted in b46ec83) and omits .github/workflows/windows.yml and Updater.kt; :12 command list omits /fav, /dropfav, /group, /dropgroup, /stats. FRIENDS.md: :7 « lien fourni par kalel95190 » (it is the releases/latest page), :30 « LINKED » (→ « connecté »), :42 formats omit MP3, :87 « Quit » (menu says « Quitter », main.js:305).
findings.proposed_change: memedrop/README.md: :193-195 → « en attente » / « connecté »; :280 → « Drops can be dragged and closed with their ✕; the rest of the window stays click-through. »; layout: remove the keystore line, add `.github/workflows/windows.yml # builds + publishes the Windows release` and `Updater.kt # in-app APK update`; :12 → append /fav, /dropfav, /group, /dropgroup, /stats. FRIENDS.md: :7 → « depuis https://github.com/Billalbzn/memedrop/releases/latest (fichier MemeDrop-Setup-x.y.z.exe) »; :30 → « connecté »; :42 → add MP3; :87 → « Quitter »; optionally one line pointing Android users to the main README section.
findings.value: Friends and the owner stop hunting for labels and files that don't exist.
